reason: The cited evidence supports entropy-driven stabilization (E2) and structural stability up to 873 K (E3), but provides no data on diffusion coefficients, sluggish diffusion kinetics, or stability above 873 K, and E1 only addresses lattice distortion scaling without linking it to diffusion barriers.
premises: High configurational entropy lowers Gibbs free energy and stabilizes the solid solution phase.
Lattice distortions from atomic size mismatch impede atomic mobility and increase diffusion activation barriers.
Sluggish diffusion kinetics in HEAs prevent phase separation and elemental segregation at high temperatures.
Diffusion coefficients in HEA nanoparticles are 1–2 orders of magnitude lower than in binary alloys.
HEA nanoparticles maintain single-phase structure and compositional homogeneity up to 1923 K.
